where: Section 1, definition of ω_z (and Exam trap 3)
problem: "positive counterclockwise when viewed along +z" is ambiguous. "Along +z" can be read as looking in the +z direction (from the origin outward), which is exactly the view that makes clockwise appear positive and reverses the sign convention the chapter relies on.
fix: "... positive counterclockwise when viewed from the +z side looking down towards the origin, that is, looking in the −z direction."

problem: This is only the tangential part of the polar vorticity. It is correct for a purely swirling field with v_r = 0, but the text never says so, so a student applying it to a flow that also has a radial component (source plus vortex) will drop a term and get the wrong answer.
fix: State the condition, or give the full form: ζ_z = (1/r) ∂(r v_θ)/∂r − (1/r) ∂v_r/∂θ, where v_r is the radial velocity in m/s; for the free and forced vortices v_r = 0, so only the first term survives.

problem: A pipe profile varies with radius r, not with a Cartesian y. Writing ∂u/∂y mixes the two systems and sits oddly next to the polar formula just above, which can confuse a student reading them together.
fix: "...so ∂u/∂r ≠ 0 (with r the distance from the axis in m, or y the distance from the wall in a thin layer near it), and every element off the axis is spinning."

problem: "...yet only one has vorticity" is too absolute. Both real flows carry vorticity somewhere; the drain flow merely comes close to an irrotational free vortex except near its rotating core. Read next to the careful statement in Section 3, the lead looks like a contradiction.
fix: "...yet only the stirred tumbler is spinning throughout; the swirling drain flow is close to an irrotational free vortex everywhere except in the rotating core at the drain."
